key_points.point: The report advocates for the rapid, automated deployment of AI-driven security operations to counter the speed of AI-enabled threats. By consolidating telemetry and automating response, defenders can achieve machine-speed containment. This approach leverages AI as a defensive force multiplier to match the operational tempo of adversaries.
key_points.verbatim: Finally, as the last line of defense, ensure the security operations center (SOC) can detect and contain threats at machine speed by consolidating telemetry and automating response.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Defenders must automate security operations and response to achieve machine-speed threat containment.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for the rapid, continuous development and deployment of advanced AI systems purpose-built for cybersecurity defense and threat mitigation. Encompasses: automated containment, machine-speed detection, and telemetry consolidation.

key_points.point: The document advocates for a structured, proactive approach to identifying and cataloging AI-driven failure modes, such as automated persona creation and AI-generated C2 instructions. By documenting these emerging threats, organizations can better anticipate and mitigate risks associated with AI-enabled tradecraft. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of building a dynamic, evolving framework for understanding AI failure modes to ensure safe and effective deployment.
key_points.verbatim: Instrument and govern AI-related activity in sensitive work?ows: Limit which AI services can interact with identities, source code or sensitive data. Log their use and investigate anomalous patterns that could indicate automated persona creation or AI-driven operations.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Countermeasures: Defending Against Nation-State Adversaries
key_points.canonical_proposition: Establish a dynamic, evolving framework for documenting and categorizing AI failure modes as they are discovered by the research community.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that establishes a dynamic, evolving framework for documenting and categorizing AI failure modes as they are discovered by the research community. Encompasses: Automated persona creation, AI-driven C2 generation, and sensitive workflow governance.

key_points.point: The document argues that defenders must deploy agentic AI to match the speed of modern adversarial attacks. By automating investigation and containment, these systems act as a 'defense accelerator' that can outpace human-led response times. This aligns with the accelerationist belief that resilience is maximized through the continuous, adaptive development of defensive AI systems.
key_points.verbatim: However, to meet the pace of modern threats, agentic AI must be deployed as the ultimate defense accelerator. These autonomous systems dynamically investigate complex alerts, correlating data across domains at machine speed to gain a complete picture.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve defensive resilience by deploying agentic AI to automate threat investigation and containment at machine speed.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for the integration of autonomous AI agents into security operations to achieve defensive superiority through machine-speed response. Encompasses: automated containment, cross-domain correlation, and dynamic threat investigation.

key_points.point: The document argues that AI and automation should be treated as core operational assets rather than mere tools. It advocates for embedding AI into business workflows to drive innovation and growth. However, it emphasizes that this must be balanced with rigorous governance to prevent systemic risk. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of leveraging AI for productivity while acknowledging the need for stable infrastructure.
key_points.verbatim: By embedding security into the fabric of your development and runtime environments, you help ensure that the speed of AI and cloud innovation drives business growth rather than systemic risk.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve business growth by embedding AI and automation into development and runtime environments while maintaining rigorous security governance.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for the integration of AI and automation into core business workflows to maximize innovation and growth. Encompasses: embedding security into development pipelines, treating AI as an operational asset, and balancing innovation speed with systemic risk management.

key_points.point: The document asserts that AI acts as a force multiplier for attackers, compressing the attack lifecycle and enabling parallelized targeting. This shift in attacker capability creates new security risks that traditional, slower-moving governance models struggle to address.
key_points.verbatim: AI has become a force multiplier for threat actors. It compresses the attack lifecycle, from access to impact, while introducing new vectors.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI acts as a force multiplier for threat actors, compressing the attack lifecycle and introducing novel attack vectors.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that identifies new and expanded security risks arising from the complex architecture and rapid deployment of AI systems. Encompasses: attack lifecycle compression, parallelized targeting, and AI-enabled tradecraft.

key_points.point: The report identifies 'Living off the AI land' (LOTAIL) as a new class of risk where attackers weaponize legitimate enterprise AI platforms. This demonstrates how the architectural complexity and integration of AI into business workflows create qualitatively new security vulnerabilities.
key_points.verbatim: Enterprise AI adoption creates a new class of risk: Living o? the AI land (LOTAIL). Just as attackers misuse PowerShell or Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI), they are now weaponizing legitimate AI platforms and embedded assistants.
key_points.excerpt_context: Trend 1. AI Has Become a Force Multiplier for Attackers
key_points.canonical_proposition: Enterprise AI adoption creates a new class of risk where attackers weaponize legitimate AI platforms and embedded assistants.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that identifies new and expanded security risks arising from the complex architecture, rapid deployment, and interconnectedness of AI systems, creating novel attack surfaces. Encompasses: LOTAIL, weaponization of legitimate platforms, and embedded assistant misuse.

key_points.point: The document asserts that the integration of SaaS, APIs, and automated workflows creates complex, interconnected architectures that introduce novel security risks. These risks are characterized by inherited permissions and opaque third-party integrations, which attackers exploit to move laterally. This supports the safetyist view that architectural complexity generates qualitatively new security risks that are difficult to monitor and control.
key_points.verbatim: SaaS environments are stitched together through OAuth apps, API keys and work?ow automation. These connections routinely carry access to data and business processes. For attackers, compromised integrations can become a lateral movement path that looks like normal automation.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, SaaS Integrations: Inherited Permissions at Scale
key_points.canonical_proposition: The complex architecture and interconnectedness of modern AI and SaaS systems create novel, expanded security risks.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that identifies new and expanded security risks arising from the complex architecture, rapid deployment, and interconnectedness of AI systems, creating novel attack surfaces. Encompasses: SaaS integrations, inherited permissions, and lateral movement paths.

key_points.point: The document highlights that rapid adoption of AI and third-party tools leads to 'inventory gaps' and 'permission opacity,' where organizations lose visibility into their own exposure. This erosion of organizational control is a direct consequence of the speed at which these systems are integrated into critical workflows. This aligns with the safetyist belief that deployment speed outpaces security governance.
key_points.verbatim: Many organizations lack a uni?ed view of SaaS connections, vendor agents and transitive libraries, slowing the answer to ôwhere is this used?ö
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, The Impact: From Response to Business Disruption
key_points.canonical_proposition: Rapid adoption of AI systems undermines security governance by creating a systemic loss of visibility and control over data and infrastructure.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that describes how the rapid adoption of AI systems undermines security governance by creating a systemic loss of visibility and control over data. Encompasses: Inventory gaps, permission opacity, and telemetry gaps.

key_points.point: The document proposes a multi-layered defense strategy, including mapping SaaS ownership, designing 'break-glass' severing plans, and hardening build ingestion. This reflects the safetyist intention to stack redundant safeguards across the entire AI and software lifecycle to mitigate the risk of cascading failures.
key_points.verbatim: Defending the supply chain requires reducing the time needed to assess exposure and the area of impact.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Countermeasures: Safeguarding the Software Supply Chain
key_points.canonical_proposition: Build defense-in-depth into AI systems by stacking redundant safeguards across the full lifecycle.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that advocates for building defense-in-depth into AI systems by stacking redundant safeguards across the full lifecycle: pre-deployment testing, runtime monitoring, and incident response. Encompasses: SaaS discovery, break-glass protocols, and build ingestion hardening.

key_points.point: The document identifies that the rapid adoption of new technologies and environmental complexity creates 'identity drift' and security gaps. Attackers exploit these inconsistencies, which arise because security governance cannot keep pace with the speed of organizational change and technology adoption. This confirms the safetyist view that deployment speed often outpaces effective security governance.
key_points.verbatim: Over time, environmental drift, driven by legacy systems, technology adoption or merger and acquisition activity, makes it di?cult to enforce a consistent standard across the enterprise.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Environmental complexity and rapid technology adoption create security gaps that outpace organizational governance.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that identifies how organizational complexity and rapid technology adoption erode security governance, leading to systemic vulnerabilities. Encompasses: environmental drift, legacy system persistence, and inconsistent control application.

key_points.point: The report highlights that identity is the primary attack surface, where excessive trust and over-permissioned accounts allow attackers to move laterally. This demonstrates that the potential damage an attacker can cause is directly proportional to the access and permissions granted to the compromised identity. This aligns with the safetyist belief that damage potential scales with system access.
key_points.verbatim: The core issue was often excessive trust — privileges and access paths that were too permissive or remained in place long after they were needed.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Excessive trust and over-permissioned accounts directly increase the potential damage of a security compromise.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that the total potential damage an AI system or compromised identity can cause scales with its access and permissions. Encompasses: excessive trust, lateral movement, and identity-related attack vectors.

key_points.point: The document mandates that AI agents and automated workflows be subjected to the same governance rigor as human users. It specifically calls for validating automation steps before production and hardening assistant accounts. This reflects the safetyist priority of defining clear authority limits and operational boundaries for autonomous systems.
key_points.verbatim: To prevent these tools from becoming vectors for attack, security teams must apply the same governance rigor to AI systems as they do to human users. This includes explicitly validating automation steps before they enter production, applying integrity checks to AI-enabled work?ows and ensuring that assistant accounts are hardened against misuse.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Apply rigorous governance, including pre-production validation and integrity checks, to all AI agents and automated workflows to prevent misuse.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates the application of strict governance and integrity validation to AI systems to prevent them from becoming attack vectors. Encompasses: pre-production validation, hardening of assistant accounts, and parity between human and machine identity governance.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes that human judgment must remain central to effective AI use to prevent governance from being bypassed. It advocates for a security culture that treats AI systems with the same discipline as critical infrastructure. This supports the safetyist intention of designing mandatory human checkpoints into AI-driven processes.
key_points.verbatim: When teams understand that human judgment remains central to e?ective AI use, governance controls are reinforced rather than bypassed, ensuring that the drive for automation does not outpace the ability to oversee it.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Maintain human judgment as a central component of AI workflows to ensure governance controls are reinforced rather than bypassed.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that advocates for the preservation of human oversight as a necessary check on automated processes. Encompasses: maintaining human judgment in AI workflows, reinforcing governance controls, and preventing automation from outpacing oversight capabilities.

key_points.point: The report documents how generative AI lowers the barrier to entry for malicious activity by providing coherence and professional polish to unsophisticated actors. This empirical observation confirms that AI tools enable actors to execute credible tradecraft with fewer human constraints.
key_points.verbatim: AI didnÆt make the attacker smarter; it just made them look professional enough to be dangerous.
key_points.excerpt_context: Trend 1. AI Has Become a Force Multiplier for Attackers
key_points.canonical_proposition: Generative AI lowers the skill barrier for producing persuasive malicious content and professional-looking extortion strategies.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that documents the empirical reality of generative AI systems producing and disseminating content designed to cause direct harm to individuals or public discourse. Encompasses: lowered barrier to entry, professionalized extortion, and AI-generated coherence.

key_points.point: The document identifies that modern business relies on 'trusted connectivity' and complex dependency ecosystems, where a single upstream compromise leads to downstream disruption. This aligns with the skeptic belief that interdependencies among components are the primary driver of systemic cyber risk, as organizations struggle to assess their exposure when a supplier is compromised.
key_points.verbatim: A single compromise can create a one-to-many opportunity, delivered through the trusted connectivity modern business relies on.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Trend 3. Software Supply Chain Attacks Increasingly Drive Downstream Disruption
key_points.canonical_proposition: Interdependencies among software and service components are the primary driver of systemic cyber risk.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that identifies interdependencies among components as the primary driver of systemic cyber risk. Encompasses: Dependency modeling, cascading failure analysis, and supply chain disruption.

key_points.point: The document notes that nation-state actors are using recruitment lures, synthetic personas, and deepfakes to target employees, effectively weaponizing human-layer interaction. This reflects the skeptic concern that surveillance and social engineering are mutually reinforcing, as attackers exploit the trust inherent in professional networks and recruitment processes to gain access.
key_points.verbatim: The result was a convincing corporate faτade designed to increase trust and improve the success rate of recruitment-driven access operations.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, North Korea: Weaponized HR Part I
key_points.canonical_proposition: Government, corporate, and third-party surveillance systems mutually reinforce each other through the exploitation of human-layer trust.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that describes the mutual reinforcement of worker surveillance through the combination of government data, corporate monitoring, and third-party data harvesting. Encompasses: Synthetic personas, recruitment lures, and deepfake identity creation.

key_points.point: The document notes that AI is being used to craft credible, error-free phishing lures that bypass traditional filters. This confirms the skeptic concern that generative AI acts as a force multiplier for social engineering, enabling attackers to scale reputation destruction and deception campaigns.
key_points.verbatim: Phishing campaigns are achieving higher conversion rates as AI helps attackers craft credible, error-free lures that bypass traditional ?lters and engage users more e?ectively.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Generative AI enables attackers to craft highly effective, error-free phishing lures that bypass traditional security filters.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that generative AI capabilities facilitate the creation of scalable, deceptive content that compromises individual and organizational security. Encompasses: phishing lure automation, filter evasion, and increased conversion rates.

key_points.point: The report observes that attackers are increasingly using business-like structures, including negotiation playbooks and brand maintenance, to conduct extortion. This reflects the skeptic view that threat actors are professionalizing, making it difficult to distinguish between legitimate business interactions and criminal activity.
key_points.verbatim: Many ransomware groups now operate with business-like structures including de?ned roles, a?liate programs and repeatable negotiation playbooks. Some cultivate ôbrand reputationö through dark web communications, portraying themselves as predictable or professional counterparts.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Ransomware groups are adopting professional business structures and brand maintenance strategies to increase the efficacy of their extortion operations.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that threat actors are professionalizing their operations to mimic legitimate business entities, thereby increasing the effectiveness of extortion. Encompasses: negotiation playbooks, brand reputation management, and affiliate programs.

key_points.point: The document advocates for active exposure management to bridge the gap between discovery and risk prioritization. It suggests filtering out noise using threat intelligence to focus on assets actively targeted in the wild. This reflects the skeptic intention of operationalizing risk mitigation through concrete, pragmatic technical practices rather than broad, theoretical frameworks.
key_points.verbatim: E?ective exposure management bridges this gap by creating a complete, continuous inventory of the digital footprint, including the shadow infrastructure and unauthorized AI tools that traditional scans miss.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Implement active exposure management by creating continuous inventories of digital footprints to prioritize and remediate exploitable, business-critical risks.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that proposes pragmatic, hands-on strategies for mitigating AI risks through continuous inventory and active exposure management. Encompasses: shadow infrastructure identification, threat intelligence-based prioritization, and remediation of exploitable risks.

key_points.point: The report argues that as organizations adopt cloud and SaaS, identity has become the practical perimeter. Attackers exploit fragmented identity estates and excessive permissions to move laterally, making identity management the most critical security focus.

The document describes a new failure mode where multiple customers are pushed into parallel triage while the upstream provider's status remains unclear. This creates a significant operational burden as teams pause changes and isolate dependencies to confirm the absence of impact.

The document notes that encryption appeared in only 78% of extortion cases in 2025, down from over 90% in previous years. Attackers are increasingly using data theft and direct pressure on partners or customers to generate leverage without needing to lock systems.

factual_claims.claim: In 2025, the fastest 25% of intrusions reached exfiltration in 1.2 hours, compared to 4.8 hours in the previous year.
Data from SaaS applications was relevant to 23% of Unit 42 investigations in 2025, compared to 18% in 2024, 12% in 2023, and 6% in 2022.
Over 60% of vulnerabilities in cloud-native applications reside in transitive libraries.
The median time to exfiltration (MTTE) for the fastest quartile of intrusions in 2025 was 72 minutes, a significant decrease from 285 minutes in 2024.
Encryption is no longer a universal feature of extortion, appearing in 78% of cases in 2025 compared to 90-96% in previous years, as attackers increasingly rely on data theft and harassment.
Identity weaknesses were a determining factor in over half of the intrusions investigated in 2025, primarily because identity stores expanded faster than the controls intended to govern them.
Software vulnerabilities accounted for 22% of initial access for incidents investigated by Unit 42 in 2025.

This allows organizations to enforce data controls in real-time regardless of the underlying hardware, effectively securing the human interface where users interact with data and AI.
